media_work.focus_or_theme: Wrongful conviction, perseverance of friendship/advocacy, flaws in eyewitness testimony.
media_work.summaryNotes: Won Audience Award at Sundance Film Festival. Based on a *This American Life* podcast episode.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Wrongful conviction, perseverance of friendship/advocacy, flaws in eyewitness testimony.

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Based on true story of Colin Warner, wrongfully convicted and spending 21 years; Focuses on friend Carl King's efforts. Directed by Matt Ruskin. Available via Amazon Prime, Digital rental.
research_notes_other.research_findings: This film dramatizes the true story of Colin Warner's wrongful conviction based largely on faulty eyewitness testimony. It particularly highlights the extraordinary dedication of his friend, Carl King, who spent years learning the legal system, tracking down witnesses, and fighting to prove Warner's innocence, eventually succeeding.

contributing_factors_raw: False/mistaken eyewitness identification, perjury by witness.
featured_individuals.status_raw: Exonerated (Conviction vacated after key witness recanted)
featured_individuals.*note: Not wrongfully convicted, but central figure)*
featured_individuals.role: Colin Warner's childhood friend who dedicated two decades to investigating the case, finding witnesses, and proving Warner's innocence.
